# GRAPH_EXPAND joins the documented StoreGraph from its root, Stores, to Locations. Sometown,
# which no store references, drops out of the LEFT JOIN, and the inlined edge SL adds no columns.
# third_party/bigquery_docs/reference/standard-sql/graph-sql-queries.md
SELECT STRING_AGG(TO_JSON_STRING(t), ',' ORDER BY S_name) FROM GRAPH_EXPAND('scalar_graph.StoreGraph') AS t
=> "{\"S_location_id\":101,\"S_name\":\"Store 1\",\"L_id\":101,\"L_name\":\"Anytown\",\"L_population\":1000},{\"S_location_id\":101,\"S_name\":\"Store 2\",\"L_id\":101,\"L_name\":\"Anytown\",\"L_population\":1000}"
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM GRAPH_EXPAND('scalar_graph.StoreGraph')
=> "2"
SELECT SUM(L_population) FROM GRAPH_EXPAND('scalar_graph.StoreGraph') GROUP BY S_location_id
=> "2000"

# BigQuery rejects COUNT(*) in a graph measure; use COUNT(column) instead (tools/bqanswers).
CREATE PROPERTY GRAPH scalar_graph.StoreGraphWithCountStarMeasure
  NODE TABLES (scalar_graph.Locations AS L
    PROPERTIES (id, population, MEASURE(SUM(population)) AS total_population,
      MEASURE(COUNT(*)) AS location_count));
=> error contains: COUNT(*) is not allowed in a measure expression in BigQuery. Please specify a column, e.g., COUNT(<column_name>).

# BigQuery inlines an edge table with its node table's table and properties only where the table
# has no columns other than those the edge references, whichever endpoint references the node
# table and whether a foreign key relates the tables; observed BigQuery answers collected with
# tools/bqanswers.
SELECT STRING_AGG(TO_JSON_STRING(t), ',' ORDER BY S_name) FROM GRAPH_EXPAND('scalar_graph.StoreGraphReversed') AS t
=> "{\"S_location_id\":101,\"S_name\":\"Store 1\",\"L_id\":101,\"L_name\":\"Anytown\",\"L_population\":1000},{\"S_location_id\":101,\"S_name\":\"Store 2\",\"L_id\":101,\"L_name\":\"Anytown\",\"L_population\":1000}"
SELECT STRING_AGG(TO_JSON_STRING(t), ',' ORDER BY S_name) FROM GRAPH_EXPAND('scalar_graph.SizedStoreGraph') AS t
=> "{\"S_location_id\":101,\"S_name\":\"Store 1\",\"S_size\":3,\"SL_location_id\":101,\"SL_name\":\"Store 1\",\"SL_size\":3,\"L_id\":101,\"L_name\":\"Anytown\",\"L_population\":1000},{\"S_location_id\":101,\"S_name\":\"Store 2\",\"S_size\":3,\"SL_location_id\":101,\"SL_name\":\"Store 2\",\"SL_size\":3,\"L_id\":101,\"L_name\":\"Anytown\",\"L_population\":1000}"

# start_node expands the subgraph reachable from that node table.
SELECT STRING_AGG(L_name ORDER BY L_id) FROM GRAPH_EXPAND('scalar_graph.StoreGraph', start_node => 'L')
=> "Anytown,Sometown"
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM GRAPH_EXPAND('scalar_graph.StoreLocations', start_node => 'S')
=> "2"

# Unflattened output exposes the selected start node's properties without label prefixes.
# Starting at L in the documented StoreGraph leaves no adjacent tables to join.
# third_party/bigquery_docs/reference/standard-sql/graph-sql-queries.md
SELECT STRING_AGG(name ORDER BY id) FROM GRAPH_EXPAND('scalar_graph.StoreGraph', start_node => 'L', flatten_results => FALSE)
=> "Anytown,Sometown"
# In the documented StoreGraph expansion, the edge is inlined and L is a top-level name.
SELECT STRING_AGG(L.name, ',' ORDER BY name) FROM GRAPH_EXPAND('scalar_graph.StoreGraph', flatten_results => FALSE)
=> "Anytown,Anytown"

# BigQuery answers collected with tools/bqanswers. Contrary to the description of nested
# STRUCTs in third_party/bigquery_docs/reference/standard-sql/graph-sql-queries.md, BigQuery
# rejects returning a joined ROW. It allows projecting scalar fields underneath it: when the
# edge is not inlined, P is nested under SP. SP survives a NULL or unmatched destination key.
SELECT TO_JSON_STRING(ARRAY(
  SELECT AS STRUCT id, SP.edge_size, SP.P.id AS place_id, SP.P.name AS place_name
  FROM GRAPH_EXPAND('scalar_graph.NestedShopPlaces', flatten_results => FALSE) ORDER BY id
))
=> "[{\"id\":1,\"edge_size\":3,\"place_id\":1,\"place_name\":\"p\"},{\"id\":2,\"edge_size\":4,\"place_id\":2,\"place_name\":null},{\"id\":3,\"edge_size\":5,\"place_id\":null,\"place_name\":null},{\"id\":4,\"edge_size\":6,\"place_id\":null,\"place_name\":null}]"
SELECT * FROM GRAPH_EXPAND('scalar_graph.NestedShopPlaces', flatten_results => FALSE) ORDER BY id
=> error contains: Returning expressions of type ROW is not allowed
SELECT * FROM GRAPH_EXPAND('scalar_graph.NestedShopPlacesDefaultEdge', flatten_results => FALSE) ORDER BY id
=> error contains: Returning expressions of type ROW is not allowed
SELECT id, P.id AS place_id, P.name AS place_name FROM GRAPH_EXPAND('scalar_graph.NestedShopPlacesDefaultEdge', flatten_results => FALSE) ORDER BY id
=> error contains: Unrecognized name: P
SELECT id, TYPEOF(P) AS place_type FROM GRAPH_EXPAND('scalar_graph.NestedShopPlacesDefaultEdge', flatten_results => FALSE) ORDER BY id
=> error contains: Unrecognized name: P

# An edge table joins between its node tables and adds its properties and key columns, ordered by
# name; a shop without a place keeps its edge row. Observed on BigQuery with tools/bqanswers.
SELECT STRING_AGG(TO_JSON_STRING(t), ',' ORDER BY S_id) FROM GRAPH_EXPAND('scalar_graph.ShopPlaces') AS t
=> "{\"S_id\":1,\"S_other_place_id\":2,\"S_place_id\":1,\"S_size\":3,\"SP_edge_size\":3,\"SP_id\":1,\"P_id\":1,\"P_name\":\"p\"},{\"S_id\":2,\"S_other_place_id\":null,\"S_place_id\":null,\"S_size\":4,\"SP_edge_size\":4,\"SP_id\":2,\"P_id\":null,\"P_name\":null}"

# Shops has columns its edges do not reference, so BigQuery joins an edge table with Shops'
# table and properties, whether it references S as its source or its destination; observed
# BigQuery answers collected with tools/bqanswers.
SELECT STRING_AGG(TO_JSON_STRING(t), ',' ORDER BY S_id) FROM GRAPH_EXPAND('scalar_graph.ShopsNear') AS t
=> "{\"S_id\":1,\"S_other_place_id\":2,\"S_place_id\":1,\"S_size\":3,\"SN_id\":1,\"SN_other_place_id\":2,\"SN_place_id\":1,\"SN_size\":3,\"Near_id\":1,\"Near_name\":\"p\"},{\"S_id\":2,\"S_other_place_id\":null,\"S_place_id\":null,\"S_size\":4,\"SN_id\":2,\"SN_other_place_id\":null,\"SN_place_id\":null,\"SN_size\":4,\"Near_id\":null,\"Near_name\":null}"
SELECT STRING_AGG(TO_JSON_STRING(t), ',' ORDER BY S_id) FROM GRAPH_EXPAND('scalar_graph.ShopsNearInlined') AS t
=> "{\"S_id\":1,\"S_other_place_id\":2,\"S_place_id\":1,\"S_size\":3,\"NS_id\":1,\"NS_other_place_id\":2,\"NS_place_id\":1,\"NS_size\":3,\"Near_id\":1,\"Near_name\":\"p\"},{\"S_id\":2,\"S_other_place_id\":null,\"S_place_id\":null,\"S_size\":4,\"NS_id\":2,\"NS_other_place_id\":null,\"NS_place_id\":null,\"NS_size\":4,\"Near_id\":null,\"Near_name\":null}"
# A node table related to two others joins each, edge then node table, in the order the graph
# defines the edge tables, whatever the order of the node tables (ShopsFarNearEdges).

=> "{\"S_id\":1,\"S_other_place_id\":2,\"S_place_id\":1,\"S_size\":3,\"SN_id\":1,\"SN_other_place_id\":2,\"SN_place_id\":1,\"SN_size\":3,\"Near_id\":1,\"Near_name\":\"p\",\"SF_id\":1,\"SF_other_place_id\":2,\"SF_place_id\":1,\"SF_size\":3,\"Far_id\":2,\"Far_name\":\"q\"},{\"S_id\":2,\"S_other_place_id\":null,\"S_place_id\":null,\"S_size\":4,\"SN_id\":2,\"SN_other_place_id\":null,\"SN_place_id\":null,\"SN_size\":4,\"Near_id\":null,\"Near_name\":null,\"SF_id\":2,\"SF_other_place_id\":null,\"SF_place_id\":null,\"SF_size\":4,\"Far_id\":null,\"Far_name\":null}"
SELECT STRING_AGG(TO_JSON_STRING(t), ',' ORDER BY S_id) FROM GRAPH_EXPAND('scalar_graph.ShopsFarNear') AS t
=> "{\"S_id\":1,\"S_other_place_id\":2,\"S_place_id\":1,\"S_size\":3,\"SF_id\":1,\"SF_other_place_id\":2,\"SF_place_id\":1,\"SF_size\":3,\"Far_id\":2,\"Far_name\":\"q\",\"SN_id\":1,\"SN_other_place_id\":2,\"SN_place_id\":1,\"SN_size\":3,\"Near_id\":1,\"Near_name\":\"p\"},{\"S_id\":2,\"S_other_place_id\":null,\"S_place_id\":null,\"S_size\":4,\"SF_id\":2,\"SF_other_place_id\":null,\"SF_place_id\":null,\"SF_size\":4,\"Far_id\":null,\"Far_name\":null,\"SN_id\":2,\"SN_other_place_id\":null,\"SN_place_id\":null,\"SN_size\":4,\"Near_id\":null,\"Near_name\":null}"

=> "{\"S_id\":1,\"S_other_place_id\":2,\"S_place_id\":1,\"S_size\":3,\"SN_id\":1,\"SN_other_place_id\":2,\"SN_place_id\":1,\"SN_size\":3,\"Near_id\":1,\"Near_name\":\"p\",\"SF_id\":1,\"SF_other_place_id\":2,\"SF_place_id\":1,\"SF_size\":3,\"Far_id\":2,\"Far_name\":\"q\"},{\"S_id\":2,\"S_other_place_id\":null,\"S_place_id\":null,\"S_size\":4,\"SN_id\":2,\"SN_other_place_id\":null,\"SN_place_id\":null,\"SN_size\":4,\"Near_id\":null,\"Near_name\":null,\"SF_id\":2,\"SF_other_place_id\":null,\"SF_place_id\":null,\"SF_size\":4,\"Far_id\":null,\"Far_name\":null}"
# A joined edge adds its key columns, not the other columns that reference its source node.
SELECT STRING_AGG(TO_JSON_STRING(t), ',' ORDER BY S_id) FROM GRAPH_EXPAND('scalar_graph.ShopSizes') AS t
=> "{\"S_id\":1,\"S_other_place_id\":2,\"S_place_id\":1,\"S_size\":3,\"SP_edge_size\":3,\"SP_id\":1,\"P_id\":1,\"P_name\":\"p\"},{\"S_id\":2,\"S_other_place_id\":null,\"S_place_id\":null,\"S_size\":4,\"SP_edge_size\":4,\"SP_id\":2,\"P_id\":null,\"P_name\":null}"

# BigQuery answers collected with tools/bqanswers: flattened output puts the second branch
# before the first branch's descendants. In nested output, C is reached through B without BC.
# A missing AB or C does not remove the unrelated AD branch.
SELECT STRING_AGG(TO_JSON_STRING(t), ',' ORDER BY A_id) FROM GRAPH_EXPAND('scalar_graph.ExpandTree') AS t
=> "{\"A_id\":1,\"AB_branch_score\":11,\"AB_id\":1,\"B_id\":10,\"B_leaf_id\":100,\"AD_sibling_score\":2,\"AD_id\":1,\"D_id\":200,\"D_name\":\"sibling\",\"C_id\":100,\"C_name\":\"leaf\"},{\"A_id\":2,\"AB_branch_score\":22,\"AB_id\":2,\"B_id\":20,\"B_leaf_id\":null,\"AD_sibling_score\":4,\"AD_id\":2,\"D_id\":200,\"D_name\":\"sibling\",\"C_id\":null,\"C_name\":null},{\"A_id\":3,\"AB_branch_score\":null,\"AB_id\":null,\"B_id\":null,\"B_leaf_id\":null,\"AD_sibling_score\":6,\"AD_id\":3,\"D_id\":200,\"D_name\":\"sibling\",\"C_id\":null,\"C_name\":null}"
SELECT TO_JSON_STRING(ARRAY(
  SELECT AS STRUCT id, AB.branch_score, AB.B.id AS branch_id,
    AD.sibling_score, AD.D.name AS sibling_name
  FROM GRAPH_EXPAND('scalar_graph.ExpandTree', flatten_results => FALSE) ORDER BY id
))
=> "[{\"id\":1,\"branch_score\":11,\"branch_id\":10,\"sibling_score\":2,\"sibling_name\":\"sibling\"},{\"id\":2,\"branch_score\":22,\"branch_id\":20,\"sibling_score\":4,\"sibling_name\":\"sibling\"},{\"id\":3,\"branch_score\":null,\"branch_id\":null,\"sibling_score\":6,\"sibling_name\":\"sibling\"}]"
SELECT TO_JSON_STRING(ARRAY(
  SELECT AS STRUCT id, AB.B.C.name AS leaf_name
  FROM GRAPH_EXPAND('scalar_graph.ExpandTree', flatten_results => FALSE) ORDER BY id
))
=> "[{\"id\":1,\"leaf_name\":\"leaf\"},{\"id\":2,\"leaf_name\":null},{\"id\":3,\"leaf_name\":null}]"
SELECT * FROM GRAPH_EXPAND('scalar_graph.ExpandTree', flatten_results => FALSE) ORDER BY id
=> error contains: Returning expressions of type ROW is not allowed

# Graphs that the documented input limitations exclude: multiple root node tables without
# start_node, and a label other than the default one.
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM GRAPH_EXPAND('scalar_graph.StoreLocations')
=> error:
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM GRAPH_EXPAND('scalar_graph.LabeledStores')
=> error:
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM GRAPH_EXPAND('scalar_graph.StoreGraph', start_node => 'Missing')
=> error:
